title: Effects of light transitions on measures of alertness, arousal and comfort
research_question: How do subjective experiences and objective measures of vigilance, arousal and thermoregulation develop over time after an acute light transition?
participant_demographics: 38 healthy subjects (19 female; Mage = 24, SDage = 2.9; range = 20-31 years old)

environmental_features.details: Abrupt transitions between two strongly contrasting light conditions: warm, dim light (CCT 2708 K, 97 lux) and cool, bright light (CCT 5854 K, 1021 lux). Transitions were WD to CB and CB to WD.
The light condition (warm, dim or cool, bright) participants were exposed to immediately prior to the experimental phase.

limitations: CCT and illuminance were manipulated simultaneously, making it impossible to attribute effects to either illuminance or CCT alone.
The study design did not allow for testing time of day as a moderator due to group sizes.
The study was a 90-minute laboratory experiment, requiring validation in longer field studies for generalizability.
